questions.question: What affects your ability to stop?
questions.correctAnswerText: The condition of the road.
questions.explanation: Road conditions greatly affect your ability to stop. Slow down when roads are slippery or in poor condition. Driving too fast on bad roads makes it hard to stop and puts you at risk.

questions.question: When you approach a railroad crossing with no flashing lights or gates, you should:

options.text: Cross the tracks immediately and as quickly as possible.
Always stop before crossing the tracks.
Be ready to yield to any train at the crossing.
Speed up to beat any oncoming train.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield to any train at the crossing.
questions.explanation: Always be ready to yield to any train before crossing railroad tracks, especially when there are no lights or gates. Do not cross until your entire vehicle can fit on the other side. Do not shift gears while crossing because your car may stall.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
Drive with caution and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign always means stop. You must come to a complete stop and check for vehicles or pedestrians before proceeding.

questions.question: What do pentagonal signs indicate?
questions.correctAnswerText: School zones.
questions.explanation: Pentagonal signs show you are in a school zone. Drive carefully and watch for children and pedestrians near schools.

questions.question: When there is a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line with the broken line next to your lane, you may pass if:
questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is clear.
questions.explanation: When the broken yellow line is on your side, you may cross to pass if there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Why should drivers be extra alert to motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?

options.text: They are difficult to see in traffic.
They obey different traffic laws than larger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are difficult to see in traffic.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians are harder to spot than cars because they are smaller and have less noticeable lights. Many crashes happen because drivers did not see them even though they were looking. Stay alert to these smaller, more vulnerable road users.

questions.question: If a green arrow turns into a solid green light, you:

options.text: May still turn, but must yield to oncoming traffic.
May no longer turn and must go straight.
Still have the right-of-way to turn.
No longer have to turn in the direction the arrow pointed.

questions.correctAnswerText: May still turn, but must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow becomes a solid green light, you may still turn in that direction. However, you must first yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane ends soon.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the right lane will end ahead.

questions.question: You must not drive faster than:

options.text: A speed that is reasonable and prudent.
A speed that is safe for current conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Drive at a speed that is reasonable, prudent, and safe for current conditions. Consider the area, traffic, pedestrians, weather, road condition, and light. Always obey posted speed limits.

questions.question: Vehicle stopping distance does NOT depend on:

options.text: The condition and type of your tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: The time of day.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on your reaction time, weather, visibility, vehicle weight, brake condition, tire condition and type, road conditions, and speed. The time of day does not affect stopping distance.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Winding road.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead has many turns and curves.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Always drive at the maximum speed limit.
Use cruise control to maintain a steady speed.
Not make any sudden changes in speed or direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not make any sudden changes in speed or direction.
questions.explanation: Avoid sudden changes in speed or direction on slippery roads. Slow down and do not use cruise control.

questions.question: An oncoming driver does not dim their high beam headlights. Where should you look?

options.text: At the wheels of the approaching vehicle.
Toward the right side of the road.
Toward the left side of the road.
Straight down the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded and lets you see enough of the road to stay on course until the other vehicle passes.

questions.question: You may be required to attend a driver improvement clinic if you accumulate ____ points against your license.
questions.correctAnswerText: Seven points
questions.explanation: If you accumulate seven points, you may have to attend a driver improvement clinic. Completing the clinic removes three points from your record.

questions.question: What color are most warning signs?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow.
questions.explanation: Most warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow with black markings. They warn drivers about unusual road conditions.

questions.question: When an oncoming car has blinding headlights, you should:

options.text: Use your bright lights until the other vehicle dims theirs.
Flash your lights on and off to warn the other driver.
Dim your lights and then speed up to pass quickly.
Look toward the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look away from the headlights and toward the right side of the road until the car passes. This keeps you from being blinded.

questions.question: You want to turn left at an intersection. The light is green but traffic is heavy. You should:

options.text: Wait at the crosswalk for traffic to clear.
Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
Turn because you have a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
questions.explanation: You may enter the intersection to prepare for your left turn if the light is green. Wait in the center until the oncoming traffic clears before you turn.

questions.question: When you see a stopped school bus on the opposite side of a center turning lane on a three-lane road, you must:

options.text: Honk your horn before passing the bus.
Continue when most kids are done exiting the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop. You may proceed when the stop arm is raised and the lights stop flashing.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, you should:

options.text: Keep the front wheel straight and set the parking brake.
Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
Turn the back wheels into the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels sharply to the left, away from the curb. If your brakes fail, your vehicle will roll into the curb instead of into traffic.

questions.question: To help prevent crashes, you should:

options.text: Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate with other road users.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do unexpected things. Tell other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians what you plan to do. Use your signals when slowing down, stopping, or turning. Use your horn when needed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop completely. Check for people and traffic crossing.
Slow down. Do not stop completely.
Stop completely. Wait for a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely. Check for people and traffic crossing.
questions.explanation: Any eight-sided sign is a stop sign. You must stop completely and look for people and traffic. Wait until the intersection is clear before you go.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: Circular signs warn of railroad crossings. This sign tells you a train crossing is coming. Look for trains before you cross the tracks.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Always stop before entering the intersection.
Yield only to traffic on the right.
Yield only to traffic on the left.
Slow down. Let other traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down. Let other traffic go first.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means slow down and let traffic in the intersection go first. You do not have to stop, but you must be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a steep downhill slope is coming.

questions.question: A school bus is stopped on the opposite side of a center turning lane on a four-lane road. Can you drive past it?

options.text: Yes, you may drive past it.
No, you must stop until the bus starts moving.
No, you must stop until the stop arm goes up.
No, you must stop until the lights stop flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, you may drive past it.
questions.explanation: When a school bus stops on the opposite side of a center turning lane on a four-lane road, you may drive past it. Still drive carefully and watch for children.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: A railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, which way should you turn the steering wheel?

options.text: Turn toward where you want the car to go.
Turn away from the direction of the skid.
Turn any direction. It does not matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn toward where you want the car to go.
questions.explanation: When your car skids, turn the wheel toward where you want the car to go. As the car straightens out, turn the wheel back the other way.

questions.question: Your car has Anti-Lock Brakes and loses traction on a slippery road. What should you do?

options.text: Press and hold the brake pedal down hard.
Press and hold the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal down hard.
questions.explanation: With Anti-Lock Brakes, press hard on the brake and hold it. The system will pump the brakes for you faster than you can. Do not pump the brakes or let go of the pedal, or the system will not work.

questions.question: How much alcohol does your body remove in one hour?
questions.correctAnswerText: About one drink an hour.
questions.explanation: Your body removes about one drink per hour. But how drunk you become depends on many things: how much you drink, how fast you drink it, your weight, if you have eaten, and your health.

questions.question: When you park downhill on a two-way street, which way should you turn your wheels?

options.text: Turn your wheels to the right.
Turn your wheels to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels to the right.
questions.explanation: When parked downhill on a two-way street, turn your wheels toward the edge of the road. If your car rolls, it will roll away from traffic.
